learning_objectives.text: Choose u and dv sensibly and evaluate integrals using integration by parts.

prerequisite_concepts.name: The substitution rule
prerequisite_concepts.relevance: Needed to rule substitution out: the student must be able to test whether one factor of the integrand is a constant multiple of the derivative of an inner function.

prerequisite_concepts.name: Product and quotient rules
prerequisite_concepts.relevance: Integration by parts reverses the product rule, and the answer can be checked by differentiating with it.

correct_approach.technique: Integration by parts with u = x and dv = cos(x) dx
correct_approach.justification: The integrand is a product of an algebraic factor and a trigonometric factor with no derivative relationship between them, so the substitution test fails. Taking u = x lets differentiation simplify it (du = dx) while dv = cos(x) dx integrates cleanly (v = sin(x)), which is the LIATE choice for this concept.

alternative_approaches.technique: Integration by parts, tabular (DI) bookkeeping: D column x, 1, 0; I column cos(x), sin(x), -cos(x)
alternative_approaches.justification: Same technique with different bookkeeping. The D column reaches 0 after one step, so the table terminates.

reference_answer: Take u = x and dv = cos(x) dx, so du = dx and v = sin(x). Then the integral of x cos(x) dx = x sin(x) - integral of sin(x) dx = x sin(x) + cos(x) + C. Check: d/dx[x sin(x) + cos(x)] = sin(x) + x cos(x) - sin(x) = x cos(x).

common_misconceptions.description: Choosing u and dv so the new integral is harder than the original.
common_misconceptions.cue: The student sets u = cos(x) and dv = x dx, and the new integral of (x^2/2) sin(x) dx is more complicated than the one they started with.
common_misconceptions.mitigation: Use LIATE and test both choices on a simple case like ∫ x e^x dx.

common_misconceptions.description: Sign errors or forgetting to integrate dv to get v.
common_misconceptions.cue: The student reports x sin(x) - cos(x) + C, or writes v = cos(x) or v = -sin(x) when dv = cos(x) dx.
common_misconceptions.mitigation: Tabulate u, du, dv, v in a 2x2 grid before substituting.

common_misconceptions.description: Reaching for u-substitution because an x sits next to a trigonometric factor, without checking whether x is a constant multiple of the derivative of an inner function.
common_misconceptions.cue: The student says they tried u-substitution (for example u = cos(x) or u = x^2) and it did not simplify.

source_reference.citation: Neuhauser, C. & Roper, M. Calculus for Biology and Medicine, 4th ed. Pearson, 2018. Section 7.2
